name: Dark Cream
lede: Dark Cream is a pale, warm yellow, ColorHub's library name for a darkened shade of [[cream]], recorded only in the xkcd color survey of 2010.

sections.title: A darkened cream
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar, "dark" plus the parent color [[cream]], itself named for the pale yellow-white of dairy cream [1]. Unlike many of the library's darkened shades, this one carries no Ridgway or ISCC-NBS filing; its only source is the crowd-sourced xkcd color survey of 2010, so the name and its boundaries rest on informal usage rather than an official dictionary [1]. On a monitor the result still reads as a light, yellow-leaning color, since "dark" here means darker than cream, not dark in any absolute sense [1].

The closest named neighbor on file is [[light-green-yellow]], with [[pastel-yellow]] a shade more vivid [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color near this swatch in only 8 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.03 per cent, among the rarer named shades in the collection, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match is a 1599 flower study, a floor and not a first, since the archive's earliest centuries are thin, and the color turns up mostly as a small highlight rather than a dominant tone [2]. These are computed color matches on photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
